findings.location: build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s52-twenty-sixth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md lines 82-92, The Appointed Texts > Responsorial Psalm (source: sections/05-appointed-texts.tex lines 93-115, two consecutive englishwitness environments)
findings.problem: The converter writes the response witness (Ps 24:6, first half) and the psalm witness (Ps 24:4-9) as two blockquotes separated only by a blank line. Python-Markdown merges them into one <blockquote>, so the site shows a single shaded quotation box where the PDF sets two separate quotation blocks. Both small-caps labels and all the text survive, and the second label still marks where the second witness begins, so no reader is misled. The difference is the loss of the semantic and visual division between two distinct quotations. The already-tracked pc-s51 edition shows the same behaviour, so the cause is in the converter.
findings.required_result: If the converter is revised, emit consecutive quotation environments as distinct blockquotes, for example by placing a non-rendering separator such as an HTML comment between them. The Responsorial Psalm's response and psalm would then render as two quotation blocks, as in the PDF, and the audit should check that each englishwitness maps to exactly one blockquote.

summary: Reviewed artifact: the canonical web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s52-twenty-sixth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md. Its conversion hash, from research/web-artifact.json, is f4803b29f75a2af149ea4af6a689b36a905504b37e5d138d15f5c939ae78c3a2. The file on disk matches that hash, and tools/web-edition regenerated the same bytes into the lane scratch area from the current sources. I compared it against the reviewed research PDF (sha256 cbdec176..., 33 pages) and the canonical TeX. All 33 render-input, PDF and aux hashes in research/artifacts.json still match. Evidence checked: (1) Text. A token diff of the PDF text against the Markdown, punctuation included, found the prose identical. The only differences were layout: running heads, page numbers, the PDF contents list replaced by [TOC], the one footnote moved to the end, the repeated longtable headers, the PDF's line-end hyphenation of branch IDs, and the H1 and description taken from the PDF's own pdftitle and pdfsubject. A word-bag check accounts for every residue. I checked the cells of the map, comparison, dossier and branch tables against the TeX, and each Date cell against research/chronology-annotations.tex. All 358 \latin, \work and \emph spans are italic, and the \notread brackets are kept. (2) Structure. The heading hierarchy follows main.tex: one H1, 11 H2 sections, 54 H3. Each of the three interpretations has its own H2 with an anchor (lane-turning, lane-two-peoples, lane-obedient-son) and closes with its own four senses. These render as three <dl> lists of Literal, Allegorical, Moral and Anagogical, 12 terms in all. The comparison and the two appendices are separate sections. There are exactly 12 proper-* anchors, one on each single-element heading, and no ids repeat. All 14 internal links resolve, and the three external URLs return HTTP 200. The footnote and its back-reference work. (3) Hygiene. There is no TeX debris, no leaked [TOC], {#...}, ** or escape text, and no model, run, path or provenance data. The Last revised (UTC) 2026-09-25T14:25:45Z timestamp and the rights colophon match the PDF. Only the canonical study is converted, with no concise or homily content, and check-web-edition confirms the eligible declaration. (4) Browser review. I rendered the page through tools/public-alpha render_page (preview mode, pinned Markdown 3.10.3, the site layout and site.css) and inspected it in headless Chromium 153 at 1280 px and at 390 px through an iframe. On desktop I looked at the title and contents, the map table, every appointed-text quotation, the lane openings, all three four-senses lists, the comparison table, the whole dossier, the branch table, the scope appendix, the references, the colophon and the footnote, and scanned the remaining prose on contact sheets. The rendered HTML text matches the Markdown with nothing consumed. At 390 px the page has no horizontal overflow. The dossier takes the site's two-by-two layout, and the map, comparison and branch tables scroll inside their own blocks as the site stylesheet intends. Limits: the browser is headless Chromium, not a physical device. The review covers only the converted text and presentation; the scholarship was accepted upstream. The generated Date-cell wording that the visual review noted ('Historical setting: Preferred In the eighth year of his reign'; 'Duration: all these nations ...') is carried over exactly from the PDF and the chronology projection. It is not a conversion defect and belongs to no owner this run admits. Verdict: PASS. The conversion is faithful and publishable. One advisory, WEB-001, concerns a merged quotation block and gates nothing.
